parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Good morning, everyone. In the last lecture, we discussed innovation in engineering design. And today I want to look at a case study. I’ll be talking about an engineering project which was recently carried out in Scotland to restore two old waterways, canals in fact, and then link them together.

I’ll talk about the design features, but first I’ll tell you a little bit about the historical background of the project. One of these canals called the Forth and Clyde opened in 1790. And it’s the oldest of Scotland’s canals. The other, the Union Canal, opened in 1822. Although the two canals were built at different levels, together they enabled vessels to travel from west to east across central Scotland. This is because the canals were connected near a town called Falkirk by a complicated system of locks which have steps and gates allowing boats to move from one level to another. However, from 1842 the two canals faced serious competition when the railway opened, which served the same cross-country route. After that they were used less and less steadily, and in the 1930s the locks at Falkirk were demolished.

Times change however. Moving on now to the turn of the millennium, Scotland embarked on an ambitious new project. The aim was to upgrade the country’s infrastructure, especially in the area of transport. There was a multi-million pound budget for this. It was a very big investment indeed. And in fact, the whole project was just one part of a long-term plan which had been developed to stimulate the national economy.

And amongst other things it involved restoring the two old canals and bringing them back into use. However, there was one major challenge as I mentioned just now. The Forth and Clyde Canal lies below the level of the Union Canal. There’s a 35-metre difference and the locks had been destroyed. So the problem was how to get boats from one level to the other. Whatever kind of solution was chosen, it was felt that it should be really innovative and imaginative.

A fitting way to mark the beginning of a new millennium. The resulting structure was a mechanical lift for boats. And because it rotates, it was called the Falkirk Wheel. The Falkirk Wheel was completed in 2002, and it was the first structure of its kind, an engineering innovation. The structure consists of two very large tanks, each large enough to contain a boat in fact. These are fixed onto opposite sides of a vertical arm. Basically, what happens is that the arm lowers one boat from the higher canal to the canal below, and at the same time it raises another boat from the lower canal to the level of the upper canal. How does this work? Well, the tanks are mounted in such a way that they stay in a horizontal plane. As one boat, together with the water that it floats in, sails into the upper tank, another floating boat simultaneously enters the lower tank. The system works on scientific principles which ensure that the weight of each boat plus the water that it floats in will be equal to the other. So once the boats have entered the tank, the arm rotates. And because the tanks are in balance, only a very small amount of energy is required for this rotation. Engineers generally agree that the Falkirk Wheel is highly functional. It’s also visually stunning. It’s an unusual shape. It looks very attractive with a lot of curves. In fact, it almost looks like a sculpture.

So where was the Falkirk Wheel manufactured? Well, it was produced entirely offsite at a place in England about 370 kilometres away. It was constructed from steel, 1,200 tons of it. It was also very strong. For example, the joints were bolted together as well as being welded. This was because a lot of stress would be placed on them by the weight of the boats and the water. Over 15,000 bolts were used and each one was tightened by hand. Of course, since it’s been in use, the design has been tested on an ongoing basis. And it may be...

Scottish case study
Project to renovate and link two canals in Scotland
Historical background
• 1790: opening of the Forth and Clyde Canal (Scotland’s canal)
• 1822: opening of the Union Canal
• The two canals allowed boats to cross the part of Scotland
• Locks (steps) connected the two canals near Falkirk
• 1842: competition from a new .
• 1930s: the locks were demolished
Millennium project
• Aim: to improve Scotland’s infrastructure.
• The long-term goal - to strengthen the Scottish .
• Involved restoration of the two canals
• Problem: one canal is 35m lower than the other
The Falkirk Wheel (a mechanical lift)
• Completed in 2002
• Two large tanks are attached to the ends of an arm
• The tanks are designed to remain in a position.
• A boat sails into each tank
• The weight of the tanks with their contents is always .
• Little energy is needed to rotate the arm

analyses.content: 录音明确提到1790年开通的Forth and Clyde是苏格兰最古老的（oldest）运河。
One of these canals called the Forth and Clyde opened in 1790. And it’s the oldest of Scotland’s canals.
你可能会因为听到年份“1790”就觉得定位结束了，但卷面上问的是这是苏格兰“怎样”的运河，必须准确抓取形容词最高级。
Although the two canals were built at different levels, together they enabled vessels to travel from west to east across central Scotland.
你可能会听到“west to east”就被干扰了，但题目卷面上填的是修饰“part of Scotland”的词，对应录音里的“central Scotland”。
录音指出这两条运河连在一起，使得船只能够自西向东横穿苏格兰中部（central）。
However, from 1842 the two canals faced serious competition when the railway opened, which served the same cross-country route.
这道题年份定位非常清晰，只要听到“1842”和“competition”这两个信号词，紧接着抓取主语名词就不会漏掉答案。
录音提到从1842年起，随着铁路（railway）的开通，这两条运河面临着严重的竞争。
The aim was to upgrade the country’s infrastructure, especially in the area of transport.
卷面上的“improve”在录音里替换成了“upgrade”，如果你死等“improve”这个词出现，极容易错过紧跟其后的目标领域。
录音说明该千年项目的目的是升级国家基础设施，特别是在交通（transport）领域。
And in fact, the whole project was just one part of a long-term plan which had been developed to stimulate the national economy.
卷面上的“strengthen the Scottish...”在录音里被同义替换成了“stimulate the national...”，你需要将“Scottish”和“national”联系起来才能准确定位。
录音提到整个项目是一个旨在刺激国家经济（economy）的长期计划的一部分。
录音解释说，水槽的安装方式使它们能够始终保持在水平（horizontal）面上。
How does this work? Well, the tanks are mounted in such a way that they stay in a horizontal plane.
卷面上的“remain in a... position”对应录音的“stay in a... plane”，如果你对这种空间位置描述的同义替换不敏感，容易在听到较长的生词时卡壳。
The system works on scientific principles which ensure that the weight of each boat plus the water that it floats in will be equal to the other.
卷面上把录音里的“each boat plus the water”高度浓缩成了“tanks with their contents”，如果你没听懂这个整体语义的概括替换，就很难抓住句末的表语。
录音指出该系统通过科学原理确保每艘船加上水的重量总是相等（equal）的。
It’s also visually stunning. It’s an unusual shape. It looks very attractive with a lot of curves. In fact, it almost looks like a sculpture.
卷面上的“resembles（类似于）”在录音里被替换成了“looks like”，这个替换非常高频，但如果拼写“sculpture”时漏掉字母“p”或拼错词尾就会白白丢分。
录音形容这个建筑看起来非常吸引人，实际上几乎就像一座雕塑（sculpture）。
It was constructed from steel, 1,200 tons of it. It was also very strong.
录音是先说了“steel”再补充了“1,200 tons”，而卷面上是“1,200 tonnes of...”，语序倒置是填空题的经典陷阱，听到数字必须要留意前后的修饰对象。
录音明确提到它是用钢材（steel）建造的，总共用了1200吨。
For example, the joints were bolted together as well as being welded. This was because a lot of stress would be placed on them by the weight of the boats and the water.
你可能会听到“weight”就想填进去，但卷面问的是为了减少什么带来的“effects（影响）”，录音里明确说这会施加大量的“stress（压力）”，真正导致负面影响的核心词是压力。
录音解释接头处不仅焊接还要用螺栓固定，是为了应对船只和水施加在它们上面的巨大压力（stress）。
